hook_text: Grapes turn into raisins, lizards warm up on rocks and plants make food. What do they all need?
clip_script: Upington. Sun, sun, sun. On the farm, grapes lie in rows. A few weeks of sunshine and: raisins! Nearby, a lizard drags itself onto a hot rock. It is cold and slow. Ten minutes of sun and it zooms off. Meerkats turn their bellies to the morning Sun. The vines catch sunlight to make sugar. And down the road, thousands of mirrors catch the Sun to make electricity. Heat and light: the Sun keeps everything alive.
visual_style: Whiteboard Orange River valley with green vineyards, trays of grapes drying into raisins in the sun, a lizard on a warm rock, a meerkat sunbathing and a house with a solar panel on the roof.
mood: Warm and sunny, like a bright summer morning.
pacing: Light for plants, then heat for animals, then how people use the Sun and stay safe in it.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list three ways the Sun helped you today.
